payload.groupTitle: FOSSIL SIDE SHELF · MOSAICS, NOT ANCESTORS
payload.compressionPrompt: Keep every fossil as a side relative or chronological constraint. Preserve anatomical uncertainty, fossil-versus-clock distinctions, current placement qualifiers, and all DOI links.

payload.body: Fossil side shelf · character combinations, not a ladder

**Shelf rule**

Every named taxon here is a side relative, branch sample, or minimum-age constraint. None is asserted to be a direct chicken ancestor. Compare character combinations and placement confidence; do not connect these cards into a smooth ancestor chain.

† **Teleocrater rhadinus · Middle Triassic**

An aphanosaur near the base of Avemetatarsalia and outside Ornithodira. Its crocodile-like ankle and body proportions show that early bird-line archosaurs did not already resemble small cursorial dinosaurs. [Nesbitt et al. 2017](https://doi.org/10.1038/nature22037)

† **Microraptor + Anchiornis · paravian flight experiments**

Microraptor preserves four long-feathered limb surfaces outside Avialae. Anchiornis preserves extensive pennaceous feathers, while its exact paravian placement varies. Neither fossil alone identifies one origin of flight. [Xu et al. 2003](https://doi.org/10.1038/nature01342); [Hu et al. 2009](https://doi.org/10.1038/nature08322)

† **Archaeopteryx · a mosaic, not ‘the first bird’**

Bone geometry supports active flapping unlike the living-bird stroke. The Chicago specimen adds palate, soft-tissue, and tertiary-feather detail; feeding-apparatus work adds a functional hypothesis, not observed behavior. [Voeten et al. 2018](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-018-03296-8); [O’Connor et al. 2025](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-025-08912-4); [O’Connor et al. 2026](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.xinn.2025.101086)

**Late Jurassic tail test**

Current best sequence: caudal count and proportional tail length declined before terminal vertebrae fused. Zhengheornis securely demonstrates the shortened, unfused stage. Whether a true pygostyle was already present depends on the disputed Baminornis element.

† **Zhengheornis buyu · secure side branch**

Late Jurassic avialan with 15 shortened caudal vertebrae and no pygostyle, estimated at roughly 74–163 g. This directly supports tail reduction before terminal fusion; it is not a chicken ancestor. [Wang et al. 2026](https://doi.org/10.1126/sciadv.aeb5202)

† **Baminornis zhenghensis? · contested side branch**

The 2025 description interpreted a fused terminal structure as the oldest avialan pygostyle. Comparative work raised a live alternative: the element may be synsacrum rather than fused tail vertebrae. Keep ‘oldest pygostyle’ conditional pending CT and independent coding. [Chen et al. 2025](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-024-08410-z); [Huang et al. 2026](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cretres.2025.106244)

† **Navaornis hestiae · enantiornithine experiment**

Its three-dimensional braincase combines ancestral and derived features. Enantiornithines were a successful Cretaceous radiation outside the living-bird line, showing that modern-looking traits were recombined on extinct branches. [Chiappe et al. 2024](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-024-08114-4)

**K–Pg ecological filter · model**

Global forest collapse may have favored ground-associated crown-bird survivors, followed by repeated arboreal re-evolution. Body size, development, diet, geography, and sampling remain possible co-causes. [Field et al. 2018](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cub.2018.04.062)

† **Asteriornis maastrichtensis · 66.8–66.7 Ma**

A latest-Cretaceous bird with galliform-like and anseriform-like cranial traits, recovered close to the galloanseran split. It constrains near-crown presence before K–Pg; it is neither the first galloanseran nor a direct chicken ancestor. [Field et al. 2020](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-020-2096-0)

† **Vegavis iaai · placement with versioned status**

A Late Cretaceous waterfowl-total-group bird. Crown-waterfowl placement was proposed in 2005, questioned in 2018, and strengthened by a nearly complete skull in 2025; precise position relative to crown Anseriformes remains worth testing. [Clarke et al. 2005](https://doi.org/10.1038/nature03150); [Mayr et al. 2018](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cretres.2018.02.013); [Torres et al. 2025](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-024-08390-0)

† **Gallinuloides wyomingensis · early Eocene**

A stem galliform that helps polarize characters near the crown. It is not a crown phasianid and not an ancestral chicken. [Ksepka 2009](https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1096-0031.2009.00250.x)
